<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **28** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fba37122b0f6646a3d8dd0b5384319e8bed3ae12` → `packageMentionDocs`.

```sh

git fetch origin bed447fa05cba2c44e69f0c6da4bfe7f246dd34e && git checkout bed447fa05cba2c44e69f0c6da4bfe7f246dd34e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fba37122b0f6646a3d8dd0b5384319e8bed3ae12
```

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a

## 席位核对

✅ ACCEPT: PR #23540 at `7d73667169` (#23359). It lands on an all-green head; no contract review is owed · 2026-10-14T20:49Z

`domain:cli` seat 2 (#22648) · `sunhaolin` · session `session_01Q9PZ5Pzqcus4woVvTZwWNU` · holder of claim `6176811990`, with the surface supplement on #23359 posted beside this record. Report: the `os-dev-report` on #23359. Thread-read: that report.

**Checklist, read against GitHub and `origin/main`, not against the report:**
- **PR shape:** draft, base `main`, title `fix(cli):`, assignee `sunhaolin`. Line 1 is `Fixes #23359`, the body's only closing keyword; line 2 is `Clause-②: no`.
- **Scope:** 6 files, +277 / −5:
  - `organization-ownership-apply.ts`;
  - one line in the command;
  - three test files;
  - one changeset.
  - `check-governed-merges --pr 23540`: NOT governed. Merge-tree is clean against `origin/main` `51b9990f47`. `ApplyOptions` is not exported from `@objectstack/cli`'s entry, so its new optional field is internal.
- **The fix, read in the diff:**
  - **The composition fact** is the boot's own answer: `stack.composition.securityPlugin`, passed as `ApplyOptions.securityPlugin`. It is never inferred from a missing name.
  - **One helper, `uncomposedSecurityRemedy`,** answers only when the plugin is known uncomposed AND the name is one its owner declares:
    - shipped sets come from `@objectstack/plugin-security`'s `securityDefaultPermissionSets`;
    - built-in positions come from `@objectstack/spec`'s `BUILTIN_IDENTITY_NAMES` + `AUDIENCE_ANCHOR_POSITIONS`.
    - It then prints `describeSecurityPluginComposition`'s own sentence plus "keep the grants / keep the bindings, and re-run where the security plugin is composed". No third spelling of the composition sentence, and no hard-coded names.
  - **Every other case keeps today's remedy:** an undeclared name, a composed run, or an unstated one.
  - **Every step still refuses.**
- **Pins and reverse verification:**
  - The 3 touched suites pass at the head (101 tests). The 6 integration files that reach the changed modules pass (195). `@objectstack/cli`'s typecheck passes.
  - Before the fix, the two extra sites went red against the two-site version.
  - **Ablation A** (the composition branch disabled) turns the 4 uncomposed pins red at their shipped-name assertion, after their unknown-name assertions held; the 4 controls stay green.
  - **Ablation B** (the command's wiring line dropped) turns the wiring pin red.
  - Both restores are proven against HEAD.
  - One throwaway real-boot measurement (`NODE_ENV=production`, no `OS_AUTH_SECRET`) read `composition.securityPlugin = { composed: false, reason: no-secret }`, and the card's two named grants and the 17.x `everyone` binding all printed the new remedy.
- **Changeset prose, sentence by sentence:** `@objectstack/cli` `patch`, `fix(cli):`, `Clause-②: no`.
  - Four FROM sentences, each the exact old remedy, and one TO for sets and one for positions; they match the diff.
  - The "Unchanged" list matches the guards: still refuses, undeclared names and composed runs keep their remedy, and other unnamed grants keep the general blocker.
- **Gates:**
  - **Local, at `7d73667169`:** the dev ran 65 derived gates: 63 run and 2 NOT MEASURED, both exit 3 on a prerequisite (no full build), which CI runs. Lint was taken as the proven narrowing.
  - **Gate evidence: the check-runs pinned to `7d73667169`, read at this stamp.** There are 37 runs: 20 `success`, 6 skipped, 11 still running, and none failed.
    - Every skip is on the expected-skip roster: Build Docs, `Dogfood Regression Gate (${{ matrix.shard }}/3)`, Temporal Conformance, Console Pin Gate, Dogfood Verify CLI, and Packed-tarball smoke.
    - Landing reads them again.
- **Contract review:** none owed. The diff touches none of the three faces: operator text in `packages/cli`, `Clause-②: no`, no schema, no governed path, no published export. CI plus this seat's read.

**Accepted deviations:**
- **Four remedy sites, not the claim's two.** The measurement falsified hypothesis (a). It also found the rewrite's unnamed legacy-grant blocker ("name or remove each", the 17.x shape) and the walled gate's binding blocker. Both are in `verifyReferences` of the same file and in the same rewrite gate, with the same cause; triage's "Never print "remove the grants" for a shipped set" applies to them. No open PR touches those regions. This seat supplements the claim's surface on #23359.
- **Two test files outside the claim's pin line.** The command's fate-supplement suite needed the composition field on its boot double, plus one wiring pin. The served-catalog suite passes the boot's `securityPlugin` and gains the composed control. Both are covered by the supplement.
- **The owners' name lists are read through a dynamic `import()` inside the helper,** honouring the claim's one-static-import-line limit, which went to `schema-migration-plugins.js`. Both are declared `@objectstack/cli` dependencies, and the idiom is the repo's own (`RestServer`'s `await import('@objectstack/spec/api')`). Accepted; a later edit may hoist them once PR #23461 has landed.
- **The composed control was measured on the `OS_AUTH_SECRET` route,** not `NODE_ENV=development`. The gate answers `{ composed: true }` on either. No committed no-secret real-boot pin: that suite costs about 23 s. The chain is pinned in three links instead.
- **Lint narrowing with three pieces of evidence.**

**Out-of-scope findings, one line each:**
- Under a wall, the rewrite gate tells the operator to resolve `authored-conversion`'s blocker for an undeclared position's binding, but that step only reports `done`. **Filed #23542**, after this PR.
- `describeSecurityPluginComposition`'s no-secret reason mentions `--dev`, a `serve` flag this command lacks. Also, the rewrite's informational note still lists a shipped-set grant without the cause; the blocker beside it now names it. **Acceptance notes**, 「承接者:无」.

**Landing:** `pr_ready` + `automerge_enable` through the relay once every check on the current head is `success` or a roster skip.
